lines: VX Drum Sequencer: a 16-step drum pattern sequencer with six voice lanes and an accent lane, sixteen pattern memories, and a polyphonic trigger output built to drive VX Drums
Chooses the memory that plays and that the grid edits; the lit button is the one playing, and while a cable is in MEM the buttons are locked and presses ignored
Cancels any hits waiting to fire and rewinds the pattern, so the next clock plays step 1, which is what a pulse at RST does
Writes a new beat into the memory playing now, each lane given a part that suits its instrument, a few ratchets sprinkled in and the memory's length kept
Advances the pattern one step per rising edge, reading high at 2V and needing a fall to 0.1V before the next edge counts; there is no clock inside, so feed it sixteenths
A rising edge cancels hits waiting to fire and rewinds the pattern, so the next clock plays step 1; a clock arriving on the same sample plays step 1 at once
Picks the memory, 0V for memory 1 up to 10V for memory 16 in steps of 0.625V; while a cable is here the memory buttons are locked and the lit one follows this voltage
Carries one voice per channel, 1 bass drum, 2 snare, 3 clap, 4 percussion, 5 closed hat, 6 open hat; every hit is a 10V pulse, 1ms long to start with, and a muted lane's channel stays silent
Carries a 10V pulse of the same length on every accented step, on the same sample as that step's hits and again with each ratchet repeat; an accented step with no hits pulses here too
Note — nothing plays until a clock pulse arrives at CLK, and unplugging the clock leaves the pattern where it stopped
Note — click a pad in the grid to place or remove a hit, and drag across pads to paint them the way the first one went; the pads are one display widget, so none of them can be clicked for help
Note — shift-click a lit voice pad to step its ratchet through x2, x3, x4 and back to a single hit, splitting the step into that many evenly spaced hits at the same strength
Note — click a lamp in the row above the grid to set the memory's length; pads past the length keep their hits and draw dimmed, and each memory has its own length
Note — click a lane label at the left of the grid to mute that lane; a muted lane neither sounds nor pulses at TRIG, and mutes are kept across a memory change
Note — the AC lane at the bottom of the grid makes every voice on that step hit harder through the kit, and makes no sound of its own
Note — two or more of these placed side by side and touching play one after another as one longer pattern; the leftmost takes the clock and reset, and every one of them carries the whole chain's hits
Note — sound design belongs to VX Drums: a memory holds the seven lanes of hits with each hit's ratchet and chance, and its length, and nothing else
Menu — Chain: head of N, or Chain: member M of N — shown only while this sequencer is part of a chain, and says which place in it this one holds; it changes nothing
Menu — Trigger length — the length of the pulses at TRIG and ACC: 1ms, 2ms, 5ms, 10ms, 20ms, 50ms, 100ms or 200ms, and every hit gets its own rising edge whichever is chosen
Menu — Randomize settings — ticks which of the seven lanes the RND button rewrites, with All and None at the bottom; an unticked lane keeps every hit it has
Menu — Chance mode — draws every lit pad as a bar whose height is its chance and lets you drag a pad up or down to set it, the top of the pad being 100% and the bottom 0%
Menu — Export pattern… — writes the memory playing now to a JSON file
Menu — Import pattern… — replaces the memory playing now with one read from a JSON file
Menu — Clear pattern — empties the memory playing now and puts its length back to 16
Menu — Ratchet ×2, Ratchet ×3, Ratchet ×4, Single, in a lit voice pad's own right-click menu — splits that step into that many evenly spaced hits, or returns it to one
Menu — Chance, in a lit pad's own right-click menu — the odds that the pad plays each time its step comes round: 100%, 75%, 50%, 25%, 10% or 0%
Menu — Copy, Paste, Clear, in a memory button's own right-click menu — puts that memory on the system clipboard, writes the clipboard into it, or empties it and sets its length back to 16

lines: Piano Roll: an eight-track note sequencer with a piano-roll editor, notes drawn on a pitch against time grid or captured as you play, and a pitch, gate and velocity output per track
Advances the pattern one sixteenth-note step per rising edge, reading high at 2V and low at 0.1V; there is no division here, so feed it sixteenths
A rising edge returns the pattern to its start and silences every voice
The pitch recorded into the active track, read as a volt per octave with 0V at C4; a monophonic cable here is used by every channel of the gate input
The gate that marks out the notes to record: a rising edge starts a note in the active track and the fall ends it, and its channel count sets how many notes can be recorded at once
The velocity recorded with each note, 0 to 10V, sampled once as that note's gate rises; unpatched, recorded notes take the default velocity
The pitch of the notes sounding on that track, a volt per octave with 0V at C4, one channel per note sounding at once
Carries 10V while a note on that track sounds, one channel per note sounding at once; back-to-back notes get a short dip between them so an envelope retriggers
The velocity of the notes sounding on that track, 0 to 10V, channel for channel with the pitch and gate; the level holds after the gate falls, so an envelope in its release reads it
Note — a track's channel count is the largest number of its notes that sound at once anywhere in the pattern, so a monophonic line gives one channel and a six-note chord six
Note — click an empty cell in the grid to paint a note, drag right while painting to set its length, drag a note's body to move it and either end to resize it
Note — the grid, the piano keys, the ruler, the velocity lane and the control bar across the top are one display widget, so none of the controls in them can be clicked for help
Note — the control bar carries SNAP, the editing grid; a scale lock; the eight numbered track squares choosing which track is edited; LOCK, which freezes editing; and REC, which arms recording
Note — recording writes what arrives at the record inputs over the top of the active track, quantised to the sixteenth grid, and captures nothing until a running clock has told it how long a step is
Note — the amber marker in the ruler is where the pattern wraps; a note starting after it is drawn as an outline and never plays
Note — click a key in the column at the left to hear that pitch through the active track's outputs, and drag up and down to slide it under one held gate; the pattern is not changed
Note — with the pointer over the grid, Delete removes the selection, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy and paste, Esc deselects and Ctrl+Z undoes; the clipboard is shared between Piano Roll modules
Menu — Lock Editor — freezes editing so the pattern cannot be painted, moved, resized, deleted, pasted, imported or recorded into; the same switch as the LOCK button
Menu — Record armed — arms recording, the same switch as the REC button
Menu — Snap: 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, Bar, Off — the grid that painting, moving, resizing and pasting land on
Menu — Loop length: 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars, 16 bars — where the pattern wraps, the same setting as the marker in the ruler
Menu — Quantize track, or Quantize selection, in the grid's own right-click menu — moves note pitches to the nearest note of a chosen root and scale, leaving their timing alone
Menu — Shift left and Shift right, in the grid's own right-click menu — rotate notes in time by a musical amount, wrapping around the loop
Menu — Select all on track, Delete selection, Delete all on track, in the grid's own right-click menu — act on the active track, leaving the other seven alone
Menu — Import MIDI... and Export MIDI..., in the grid's own right-click menu — read a standard MIDI file over the pattern, quantised to the sixteenth grid, or write the pattern out as one

piano_roll.notes: Written against the v2.47.0 release commit 4588d09, the installed build. The maker's manual names the jacks CLK, RST, REC V/O, REC GT and REC VEL; the panel prints CLOCK, RESET, and a RECORD group of CV, GATE and VEL, and the panel is what is written here. The panel render in the maker's documentation is stale — it shows two output jacks per track and no record velocity jack, where the installed panel has three per track and the velocity jack. lines: Timeline: a 16-lane automation sequencer. Draw a control curve of nodes joined by straight or bent segments against bars and beats, and play all sixteen lanes out of one polyphonic cable
Sets the tempo every lane runs at, 20 to 300 BPM in half-BPM steps; there is no clock input, so this is where the module's timing comes from
Turned on, playback wraps at the loop end, which is the drawn content rounded up to a whole bar, or four bars on an empty timeline, unless the amber handle in the ruler has been dragged
Turned on, the view follows the selected lane's playhead and keeps it centred; panning or paging the scrollbar suspends it until you seek, the loop wraps, or the playhead comes back on screen
Starts and stops every lane at once; between flips of this switch the START and STOP inputs set each lane's state on its own
Rewinds every lane to the beginning
Arms recording, lighting red while armed; a take runs whenever the transport is also playing, and arming while stopped does nothing until play starts
A trigger starts a lane playing; a monophonic cable starts every lane, and on a polyphonic cable channel 1 starts lane 1, channel 2 lane 2 and so on, leaving lanes past the channel count alone
A trigger stops a lane where it is; a monophonic cable stops every lane, and on a polyphonic cable channel 1 stops lane 1, channel 2 lane 2 and so on
A trigger rewinds a lane to the beginning; a monophonic cable rewinds every lane, and on a polyphonic cable channel 1 rewinds lane 1, channel 2 lane 2 and so on
The voltage written into a lane while a take runs: a monophonic cable records into the selected lane, and a polyphonic one records channel 1 into lane 1, channel 2 into lane 2 and so on
A clock taken from each lane's playhead, one channel per lane, at the division the Clock division menu item sets
A trigger on each lane's rewind and on each loop wrap, one channel per lane; this is the one to patch into a downstream sequencer's reset
A trigger on each lane's rewind only, one channel per lane; a loop wrap does not fire it
A trigger on each loop wrap only, one channel per lane
Carries 10V while that lane is playing and 0V while it is stopped, one channel per lane
The sixteen automation curves, -10V to 10V, one channel per lane; an empty lane carries 0V
Note — a lane with no nodes drawn in it carries 0V and does nothing; click in the editor to place the first node, then drag it into position
Note — the curve editor, the ruler, the loop handle and the sixteen lane tabs above it are one display widget, so none of the controls in them can be clicked for help
Note — in the editor, click empty space to add a node, drag a node to move it, right-click a node to delete it, and drag the diamond on a segment to bend it; right-click the diamond to straighten it
Note — the numbered tabs above the editor choose the lane shown; a tab with nodes in it reads brighter, and each carries a dot that is green while its lane runs and red while it is stopped
Note — a take starts on the first sample where the REC button is armed and a target lane is playing, ends when either stops, and writes only over the part of the lane the playhead passes
Note — a lane holds at most 8192 nodes; a take that reaches the limit stops adding them and a red LANE FULL notice appears beside the readout
Note — a curve holds its first node's value before that node and its last node's value after it, so a lane has a voltage everywhere
Menu — Lock Editor — freezes the editor against mouse edits and tints it red, clicks falling through to the panel; recording goes on working while it is locked
Menu — Snap: Off, 1 bar, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 — the grid that node placement and the loop handle land on. Recording ignores it
Menu — Clock division: 1/1 (bar), 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 — the division of each lane's beat that the CLK output carries
Menu — Record rate: 1 bar, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 — the grid a take samples the REC input on; a node is written only where the value changes
Menu — Clear lane, in the editor's own right-click menu — removes every node from the selected lane
Menu — Straighten lane, in the editor's own right-click menu — removes every bend from the selected lane, keeping its nodes
Menu — Fit view to content, in the editor's own right-click menu — zooms the editor to show everything drawn in the selected lane
Menu — Reset zoom, in the editor's own right-click menu — returns the editor to its default view
